app_note: Sucrose is the standard table sugar molecule.
risk_note: Added sugar intake should be shown separately from natural occurrence.

app_note: Glucose is a basic sugar used by living cells.
risk_note: Can raise blood glucose quickly.

app_note: Dextrose is typically glucose produced from starch.
risk_note: Often corn-derived in North America.

app_note: Fructose tastes sweeter than sucrose in many uses.
risk_note: High intake context differs from whole fruit.

app_note: Corn syrup helps candies stay smooth by limiting sugar crystallization.
risk_note: Different from high-fructose corn syrup.

app_note: HFCS is corn syrup enzymatically adjusted to contain more fructose.
risk_note: Controversial mostly because of added-sugar intake patterns.

app_note: Honey contains sugars plus trace aroma compounds from flowers.
risk_note: Not for infants under one year.

app_note: Maple syrup is concentrated sap from maple trees.
risk_note: Still mostly sugar despite natural origin.

app_note: Molasses is a byproduct of sugar refining with dark flavor.
risk_note: Strong flavor and high sugar content.

app_note: Agave syrup is usually high in fructose relative to table sugar.
risk_note: Natural branding should not imply unlimited use.

app_note: Stevia sweetness comes from steviol glycosides in stevia leaves.
risk_note: Use approved extract status rather than whole-leaf assumptions.

app_note: Monk fruit sweetness comes from mogrosides.
risk_note: Often blended with erythritol or other carriers.

app_note: Aspartame is made from amino-acid related components.
risk_note: Requires phenylalanine warning for PKU contexts.

app_note: Sucralose is much sweeter than sugar and often used in tiny amounts.
risk_note: Needs temperature and evidence wording reviewed.

app_note: Saccharin is one of the oldest artificial sweeteners.
risk_note: Historical controversy needs careful updated context.

app_note: Often combined with other sweeteners to balance flavor.
risk_note: Needs source-backed safety context.

app_note: Neotame is chemically related to aspartame but used at very low levels.
risk_note: Needs review for market availability.

app_note: Advantame is an extremely high-potency sweetener.
risk_note: Needs jurisdictional review.

app_note: Erythritol provides bulk with fewer calories than sugar.
risk_note: Recent research claims need careful non-alarmist handling.

app_note: Xylitol is common in sugar-free gum.
risk_note: Extremely dangerous to dogs; app can flag pet-safety warning.

app_note: Sorbitol can help foods retain moisture.
risk_note: Large amounts may cause laxative effects.

app_note: Mannitol is a polyol used for mild sweetness and texture.
risk_note: Large amounts may affect digestion.

app_note: Maltitol behaves more like sugar in texture than many polyols.
risk_note: Can cause digestive discomfort in larger amounts.

app_note: Allulose is a rare sugar used in newer low-sugar products.
risk_note: Regulatory status varies by jurisdiction.

app_note: Isomalt is useful for hard candies and decorative sugar work.
risk_note: Can have laxative effects in high amounts.
